title: Facile radiolabeling of monoclonal antibodies and other proteins with zirconium-89 or gallium-68 for PET imaging using p-isothiocyanatobenzyl-desferrioxamine
protocol: Pipette the required amount of protein solution into an eppendorf tube.
Adjust the reaction mixture to a total volume of 1 ml by adding normal saline.
Adjust pH of the protein solution to pH = 8.9 – 9.1 with 0.1 M NaCO.
Dissolve SCN-Bz-Df in DMSO at a concentration of between 2 and 5 mM depending on the amount of protein or antibody used.
Add this to the protein solution to give a 3-fold molar excess of the chelator over the molar amount of protein and mix immediately.
Incubate the reaction for 30 min at 37°C using a Thermomixer.
Rinse a PD10 column with 20 ml 0.9% NaCl/gentisic acid 5 mg/ml (pH = 4.9-5.3).
Pipette the conjugation reaction mixture onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 1.5 ml 0.9% NaCl/gentisic acid 5 mg/ml (pH = 4.9-5.3) onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 2 ml 0.9% NaCl/gentisic acid 5 mg/ml (pH = 4.9-5.3) onto the PD10 column and collect the Df-protein.
Store the collected Df-protein at -20°C until the day of planned use.
Pipette the required volume of <sup>89</sup>Zr oxalic acid solution into a glass "reaction vial".
While gently shaking, add 200 μl of 1M oxalic acid to the reaction vial.
Add 90 μl of 2 M Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> to the reaction vial and incubate for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Pipette 0.30 ml of 0.5 M HEPES (pH = 7.2) into the reaction vial.
Pipette 0.71 ml of modified protein (typically 1-3 mg) into the reaction vial.
Pipette 0.70 ml of 0.5 M HEPES (pH = 7.2) into the reaction vial.
Incubate the reaction mixture for 1 hour at room temperature while gently shaking.
Rinse a PD10 column with 20 ml of 0.9% NaCl/gentisic acid 5 mg/ml (pH = 4.9-5.3).
After 1 hour, pipette the reaction mixture onto the PD10 column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 1.5 ml of 0.9% NaCl/gentisic acid 5 mg/ml (pH = 4.9-5.3) onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 2 ml of 0.9% NaCl/gentisic acid 5 mg/ml (pH = 4.9-5.3) to the PD10 column and collect the purified radiolabeled protein.
Analyze the purified radiolabeled protein by ITLC and HPLC.
When the radiochemical purity is greater than 95%, store the protein at 4°C or dilute it in 0.9% NaCl/gentisic acid 5 mg ml^-1 (pH = 4.9-5.3) for use.
Rinse a PD10 column with 20 ml of 0.25 M ammonium acetate (pH = 5.5).
Pipette the conjugation reaction mixture onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 1.5 ml of 0.25 M ammonium acetate (pH = 5.5) onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 2 ml of 0.25 M ammonium acetate (pH = 5.5) onto the PD-10 column and collect the Df-protein.
Store the Df-protein at -20°C until use.
Pipette the required volume of preconcentrated and purified ^68Ga into a 5 ml test tube.
While gently shaking, add 2 x ________\(= **a**, see v.) = _________ μl 3 M ammonium acetate into the reaction vial and incubate for 3 minutes at room temperature.
While gently shaking, slowly add 0.2-1.0 ml of the modified protein (typically 0.5-2 mg) into the reaction vial.
Adjust the reaction mixture to a total volume of 1.5 ml by adding a sufficient amount of 0.25 M ammonium acetate (pH = 5.5) into the tube.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature while gently shaking the reaction mixture.
Rinse a PD10 column with 20 ml normal saline.
After 5 min incubation, pipette the reaction mixture onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 2.0 ml normal saline onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 1.5 ml normal saline onto the PD-10 column and collect the purified radiolabeled protein.
Analyze the purified ^68Ga-labeled protein by ITLC.
Analyze the purified ^68Ga-labeled protein by HPLC.
Activate a Chromafix 30-PS-HCO₃ cartridge with 1 ml of 100% ethanol.
Wash the activated cartridge with 1 ml of Milli-Q water.
Wash the cartridge with 1 ml of 4 M HCl.
Elute the ^68Ge/^68Ga-generator with 0.1 M HCl according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Collect the generator eluate and add enough 30% HCl to achieve a final concentration of 4.0 M HCl.
Slowly load the eluate onto the activated Chromafix cartridge at a flow rate of 0.5-1 ml/min.
Discard the flow-through from the cartridge.
Wash the cartridge with 2 ml of 4 M HCl.
Dry the cartridge by sucking air through it.
Elute the purified and concentrated ^68Ga in small fractions of Milli-Q water (50-100 μl).
Measure the activity of the collected fractions.
